prompt:
Search the web now. You are a financial fact extractor for a US-equity pre-market brief.
Brief date: Friday October 16, 2026. Story: OpenAI / Trail of Bits Acquisition Talks: Catalyst for CRWD, PANW, OKTA, ZS Selloff. Related tickers: CRWD, PANW, OKTA, ZS, FTNT.

Window: Thursday October 15, 2026 regular session (9:30-16:00 ET) through Friday October 16, 2026 02:03 ET, including after-hours, overnight and pre-market news. Anything published after 02:03 ET on Friday October 16, 2026 is out of scope.

Why this needs follow-up: Cybersecurity names CRWD (-3.3%), PANW, OKTA, ZS, and FTNT all fell 1.5%-3.3% on an unconfirmed report that OpenAI was in early talks to acquire Trail of Bits — the deal terms, confirmation status, and which analysts specifically named these as losers needs verification.

ANSWER EACH QUESTION (run a separate search for each):
- What is the source and current status of the report that OpenAI was in early talks to acquire Trail of Bits as of October 15 2026, and has either party confirmed or denied it?
- Which analysts on October 15 2026 explicitly cited the OpenAI-Trail of Bits report as the catalyst for the cybersecurity sector selloff, and did any name specific revenue-at-risk estimates?
- What is Trail of Bits' annual revenue, valuation, and product overlap with CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, and Zscaler that would justify a competitive threat thesis?

Name every stock affected by this story with its move, analyst notes that name winners and losers
(firm, rating, PT), exact figures (deal values, estimates, dates), and the latest status as of the
cutoff. Prefer Reuters, Bloomberg, CNBC, WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch, company releases, filings.

OUTPUT (markdown; no intro or conclusion). Group by ticker or sub-topic:

## TICKER or Sub-topic `[Category]`
- fact (source)

RULES
- Facts only. Every bullet has a specific number, name, or date. No bullet without a data point.
- End every bullet with the named source and publish time if known: (Reuters, Sep 24 07:12 ET).
  Convert every time to ET (ET = GMT-4 / UTC-4 in EDT; 09:59 GMT = 05:59 ET) before judging whether
  it is inside the window. For prices quoted several times, report the latest reading before the
  cutoff with its time.
  "Analysts said" / "reports suggest" without a name is not allowed.
- Earnings: actual vs consensus for EPS and revenue; guidance old → new.
- Analyst actions: firm, rating old → new, PT old → new.
- Mark unconfirmed items (people familiar, leaks, social media, M&A speculation) with [rumor]. A
  Bloomberg/Reuters/WSJ report citing sources is still reportable: state it and mark [report].
- If one event moved several stocks, name every stock and its move in the same bullet.
- Only facts published in the window. Older background only if it is the direct cause of a move in
  the window, labelled with its date.
- Do not interpret price action. Do not write "strong", "beat expectations", "investors cheered",
  "remains", "continues to", "well-positioned", "tailwinds". Write the number.
- Do not write bullets about what you could not find. Omit the topic instead.
- Do not drop facts to save space.
content:
## Report status `[OpenAI / Trail of Bits]`
- [rumor][report] The Information reported on October 14 that OpenAI was in early discussions to acquire New York-based software-security company Trail of Bits; no purchase price or transaction terms were disclosed, and the talks could still fail. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 14, updated Oct. 15; publication time not provided)[6]
- OpenAI and Trail of Bits had not publicly confirmed or denied the discussions as of October 15; the reported talks remained unconfirmed. (Crypto Times, Oct. 14; publication time not provided)[8]
- OpenAI and Trail of Bits had previously launched the “Patch the Planet” initiative in June 2026; the project had identified 1,917 issues across 67 codebases and resulted in 462 upstream patches, according to the report. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 14, updated Oct. 15; publication time not provided)[6]
- Trail of Bits was founded in 2012, had more than 40 employees, and focused on security research, vulnerability discovery, open-source-code remediation, and software-security audits. (Crypto Times, Oct. 14; publication time not provided)[8]

## CRWD `[Stock move / analyst notes]`
- CrowdStrike fell 3.16% on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]
- CrowdStrike fell about 3% in the October 14 trading report tied to the OpenAI acquisition story. (Investors.com, Oct. 14, updated Oct. 15, 10:21 ET)[3]
- Citi analyst Fatima Boolani maintained a Buy rating and raised CrowdStrike’s price target to $295 from $260 on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]
- The October 15 report did not identify a named analyst who assigned a specific CrowdStrike revenue-at-risk estimate to the Trail of Bits report. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]

## PANW `[Stock move / analyst notes]`
- Palo Alto Networks fell 2.76% on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]
- Palo Alto Networks declined nearly 3% in the October 14 report tied to the OpenAI acquisition story. (Investors.com, Oct. 14, updated Oct. 15, 10:21 ET)[3]
- Citi analyst Fatima Boolani maintained a Buy rating and raised Palo Alto Networks’ price target to $440 from $410 on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]
- The October 15 report did not identify a named analyst who assigned a specific Palo Alto Networks revenue-at-risk estimate to the Trail of Bits report. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]

## OKTA `[Stock move / analyst notes]`
- Okta fell 3.33% on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]
- Citi analyst Fatima Boolani maintained a Neutral rating and raised Okta’s price target to $215 from $205 on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]
- The October 15 report did not identify a named analyst who assigned a specific Okta revenue-at-risk estimate to the Trail of Bits report. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]

## ZS `[Stock move / analyst notes]`
- Zscaler fell 1.50% on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]
- Citi analyst Fatima Boolani maintained a Buy rating and raised Zscaler’s price target to $260 from $245 on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]
- The October 15 report did not identify a named analyst who assigned a specific Zscaler revenue-at-risk estimate to the Trail of Bits report. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]

## FTNT `[Stock move / analyst notes]`
- Fortinet fell 2.91% on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]
- Fortinet closed down 3.52% at $184.05 in the October 14 trading session covered by the October 15 report. (The Arabian Post, Oct. 15; publication time not provided)[4]
- Wells Fargo analyst Richard Poland maintained an Underweight rating and raised Fortinet’s price target to $160 from $135 on October 15. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]
- The October 15 report did not identify a named analyst who assigned a specific Fortinet revenue-at-risk estimate to the Trail of Bits report. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]

## Analysts and catalyst `[Sector]`
- The October 15 report named Citi analyst Fatima Boolani and Wells Fargo analyst Richard Poland, but both published positive or unchanged rating actions rather than a quantified revenue-at-risk estimate tied to the Trail of Bits report. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]
- The reported acquisition was described as a source of renewed competition concerns for cybersecurity stocks, while Citi cited ten channel-partner discussions and a reseller survey indicating improving cybersecurity spending into 2027. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]
- No named analyst or source in the retrieved October 15 material provided a dollar revenue-at-risk estimate for CRWD, PANW, OKTA, ZS, or FTNT from the reported acquisition. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 15, 18:02 GMT+6; 08:02 ET)[1]

## Trail of Bits `[Financials / competitive overlap]`
- No annual-revenue figure or valuation for Trail of Bits was disclosed in the retrieved October 14-15 reports; no transaction value was reported. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 14, updated Oct. 15; publication time not provided)[6]
- Trail of Bits’ reported products and services included open-source vulnerability detection and remediation, security research, software audits, and tools including Slither and Echidna. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 14, updated Oct. 15; publication time not provided)[6]
- Trail of Bits had audited or served crypto and blockchain projects including Uniswap, Aave, Arbitrum, Worldcoin, Offchain Labs, and Gensyn. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 14, updated Oct. 15; publication time not provided)[6]
- CrowdStrike specializes in endpoint security and threat detection, Palo Alto Networks sells network, cloud, and identity protection, and Zscaler provides cloud-delivered controls for application and data access. (The Arabian Post, Oct. 15; publication time not provided)[4]
- The retrieved reports described Trail of Bits as a security-research and software-audit company, but did not provide quantified product overlap, customer overlap, annual revenue, valuation, or addressable revenue exposure relative to CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, or Zscaler. (Yahoo Finance, Oct. 14, updated Oct. 15; publication time not provided)[6]
